Kalman Filter — 2D Tracking Lab

State: [x, y, vx, vy] · Constant-velocity model · Position measurements only

Controls

Tips:
· High R → filter trusts model more → smoother but slower.
· High Q → filter trusts measurements more → noisier but responsive.
· Ellipse = 95% position uncertainty.

How the Kalman Filter Works

The Kalman filter maintains a Gaussian belief over the hidden state x = [x, y, vx, vy]. Each time-step has two phases:

Predict
x̂⁻ = F · x̂
P⁻ = F · P · Fᵀ + Q
Update
K = P⁻ · Hᵀ · (H · P⁻ · Hᵀ + R)⁻¹
x̂ = x̂⁻ + K · (z − H · x̂⁻)
P = (I − K·H) · P⁻

Matrices used here:

F — state transition (constant-velocity).
H — measurement model: observes x,y only.
Q — process noise covariance (controls model uncertainty).
R — measurement noise covariance (sensor noise level).
P — state covariance (the ellipse you see).
K — Kalman gain: blends prediction vs. measurement.

The blue ellipse is the 2σ contour of the marginal position covariance — it shrinks when the filter is confident and expands when measurements are noisy or absent.
